A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of the immune response to Leptospira infection is complex and involves a fine balance of pro- and anti- inflammatory effectors.

we have demonstrated the relevance of studying immune gene expression in a hamster LD50 model of Leptospira infection, as well as the relevance of using a LD100 or a high-passage non-virulent variant of L. interrogans to validate the expression of these genes in a nonlethal model of infection.

the immune response of hamsters with severe leptospiosis is characterized by an up-regulated expression of both pro-inflammatory (TNFα, IL-1α, and COX-2) and anti-inflammatory (IL-10) mediators, which may contribute to a higher susceptibility to infection and to the development of severe leptospiroses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory genes should be considered to better understand the evolution of leptospiraemic infections and to identify new biomarkers.
the expression levels of immune genes could be used to predict the evolution of the infection.
